title: Canary upgrade orchestration: version contracts + mirrored health probes for private control planes
creator: Avery Chen
description: Introduce a guarded canary promotion flow for Private (VPC) control plane upgrades that uses explicit version contracts and a mirrored health-probe observer. Goal: allow safe progressive promotions across tenants with deterministic rollback triggers while minimizing blast radius and operator intervention. Scope: Terraform module changes for canary routing, an observer deployment that mirrors health probes (no product traffic), gating rules driven by telemetry (latency / error / reconciliation success), and an operational runbook for emergency cutovers. This ticket focuses on orchestration and safety gates; per-tenant traffic slicing and tenant-specific policies will be follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes canary target groups and a traffic-mirroring toggle with minimal surface area for existing Private customers
Control plane operator can launch a versioned canary cohort using the console or CLI (API documented)
Observer pods mirror health probes and emit the same telemetry to the console without serving production traffic
Automatic promotion triggers: p95 control-plane reconciliation latency < 150ms AND 1-minute error rate < 0.5% for 10m window
Automatic rollback trigger on any critical reconciliation failure or sustained error rate > 1.5% for 5m
End-to-end test coverage (unit + integration) and a canary runbook with rollback checklist
Security review completed and KMS/HSM compatibility verified for version artifacts
implementation_notes: Add 'canary_group' and 'observer_group' resources to terraform/modules/private-controlplane; keep defaults disabled to prevent accidental activation
Introduce 'version_contract' metadata on control plane manifests that enumerates compatible runtime components and migration steps

Observer architecture: create lightweight, read-only pod set that subscribes to the same health checks (liveness/probe endpoints) and mirrors results to telemetry pipeline with a dedicated tag 'canary_observer'
Routing: use traffic-mirroring (not routing) for observer; production tenant traffic continues to the current version while observer probes target candidate versions

Gating service: implement gating lambda inside control plane operator that evaluates sliding-window metrics (prometheus query) and outputs a deterministic decision (promote/hold/rollback), expose decision events to console
Terraform plan output must include explicit approval step for promotions when 'manual_promote' == true
Tie canary lifecycle to release artifacts stored in immutable artifact registry; record artifact digest in controlplane state for verifiable rollbacks
Backward compatibility: ensure new control plane versions support prior storage schema for at least N+1 releases or include automatic migration hooks with a dry-run flag
test_plan: Unit tests for gating logic and contract validation (CI)
Integration: create ephemeral VPC clusters in staging, run canary promotion with observer enabled, assert no production traffic diverted
Chaos tests: network partitions and intermittent API server failures — verify automatic rollback and operator alerts
Load test: simulate tenant reconciliation at expected peak QPS to validate p95 latency thresholds and autoscaler behavior
Dry-run upgrade: run promotion with 'mirror-only' mode and validate observer telemetry matches golden baseline within tolerance
Runbook verify: simulated rollback procedure executed by on-call engineer in staging and time-to-recovery measured

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Observer probe could add load to candidate version and skew results — Mitigation: limit probe QPS and use rate-limiting + dedicated resources
Risk: Misconfigured Terraform toggles accidentally enable canary in production — Mitigation: default disabled, require two-step approval and a 'safety_hard_stop' flag in state

Risk: Telemetry signal noise causing false-positive rollback — Mitigation: use multiple complementary signals (reconciliation success, errors, controller restarts) and require sustained violation windows
Risk: Artifact signing or KMS issues during rollback — Mitigation: pre-validate key policies and include a manual rollback fallback that uses last-known-good digest
